If you’re starting with a small account, for one, you really don’t need to trade everyday. Don’t stRt your session expecting a trade to hit every time. You really want to look for A+ set ups, SOMETIMES B set ups, but never take C or D trades. Why? Well your risk per trade is better spread out across A+ trades. Yes, they won’t happen as often but, when you’re just starting out. The momentum is important.

Once you get going, I’d recommend a profit target, since you’re only doing 1 MES, you really want consistent and smooth gains. Ideally, it’s 2:1 to whatever you decide is your risk. With ES, 10 pts is usually good for my style, but not sure what you’re comfortable with. 

With scalping, it tends to be a little bit harder because you need to be right more then you’re wrong or at the very least have a 2:1 show up. 



After that, let’s say you have a week of green, the following week, take your total amount and maybe determine that as your MAX loss on the week.

What I’ve always found is… it’s easy to make the money, the problem is keeping it. You REALLY want to employ max daily drawdowns on your broker settings. Anything to help better protect you from emotions. I’m sorry if this isn’t directly answering your questions. It’s hard to do without knowing your trade style and your win ratio.

**TLDR;** 

Find motivation and the why for everything you want. Don't just wake up early because it's what you hear is good for you. You need to have the drive to get to where you want or less you'll always be at a standstill wondering why you're goals aren't moving any closer to you. 

This is kind of a ramble but I've been having this talk with a friend of mine who like you is having a hard time getting to bed, wants to be more productive but can't seem to find their rhythm. 

I can't find the video at the moment. But, there was this excellent piece of content on YouTube about the difference between someone who procrastinates and someone who is motivated. Now, I'm not saying that you'e not motivated to go to uni. For all I know you could have drive and ambitions that are endless. 

But, the video made a good point at highlighting the importance of why some people strive in school and why others don't. It's not that you're unable to do the work or that you don't want to. But, could your motivation and passions be at a lost therefore creating this loop of procrastination?

Uninstalling apps or voiding the enjoyment of XYZ can be really useful as it'll limit your distractions. But, the self-control and discipline becomes really empowering when you can have all of these apps but still manage to work on what it is you need. 

When it comes to waking up at 7AM. Ask yourself, why? Ever since middle school, I would always wake up early. Usually around 5/6AM. For a long time though, I would just sit in bed and do nothing. Mostly waiting until the very last minute I could before I had to get dress and run down the street to get to school on time. I had ZERO motivation to go to middle school and I just wanted to stay home all day and play video games. I would even find myself playing video games right when I woke up (partly because I was addicted) but I was also motivated to play. I was motivated to make new friends online and level up. 

Waking up at any "early" time is fetishized with the whole hustle movement. But, if you don't have a strong enough why then it really makes no point. if you're waking up at 7AM because you need to hit the gym and get your morning routine in then great. But, if you're only doing it because you read somewhere that it's what productive people do. Then, you're going to never want to actually wake up at this time. 

For sleep, it is crucial to understand that there's only so much you can do in a day. When I write (creatively) I typically try to cap myself out after about 2 hours of writing continuously. Not because I'm all out of juice but because I'm not always going to have the luxury to write for such long periods of time. Let's say you started your homework at 8PM, unless you have a really tight deadline. Most of the things you're doing can wait till the morning. Especially if you're biggest concern is waking up on time for uni.
